content.text:
The Australian raven has adapted to cities in several ways:

- **Flexible diet:** It is an omnivorous, opportunistic feeder and readily scavenges **food waste** in urban areas. [passage-00016828]
- **Use of built structures:** Although it usually nests high in trees, it can also nest on **man-made structures**, including windmills and buildings. [passage-00016828]
- **Tolerance of urban living:** These adaptations have enabled it to become a **common city bird** in Sydney, Canberra, and Perth. [passage-00016828]

The indexed evidence supports these points, but does not provide much detail on other possible urban adaptations, such as changes in nesting timing or responses to traffic and human disturbance.
